title: Agreement of trait specializations of a semiabelian homomorphism
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $P,Q\to S$ be smooth separated commutative group schemes of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with semiabelian geometric fibres. All group operations are morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Semiabelian geometric fibres have the meaning of [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Write $\eta$ for the generic point, $K=\kappa(\eta)$, and fix a $K$-group homomorphism $u:P_\eta\to Q_\eta$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For $i=1,2$, let $R_i$ be either a field or a discrete valuation ring [def-weil-field, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $L_i$, residue field $k_i$, and a morphism $a_i:\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to S$ whose generic point maps to $\eta$ and whose closed point maps to the same point $s\in S$. Suppose $v_i:P\times_S\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to Q\times_S\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ are group homomorphisms restricting to the base change of $u$ over $L_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\Omega$ be any algebraically closed field and $\kappa(s)$-embeddings $k_i\hookrightarrow\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-field-extension]. Then the induced homomorphisms on the common geometric fibre agree: $$(v_1)_\Omega=(v_2)_\Omega:P_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\Omega\longrightarrow Q_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\Omega.$$ The extensions $v_i$ are hypotheses; the conclusion asserts only agreement of their specializations, not existence over $S$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$. Both trait maps give local injections $A\to R_i$: their generic points map to $\eta$, so a nonzero element of the domain $A\subset K$ cannot map to zero. Normality of $S$ makes $A$ a normal domain. Use [lem-sfb-normal-strict-local-trait-lifts] with the specified embeddings in $\Omega$ to obtain the same strict henselization $H$ of $A$, strict henselizations $B_i$ of $R_i$, and injective local maps $H\to B_i$. Write $F=\operatorname{Frac}H$ and $F_i=\operatorname{Frac}B_i$; these maps embed $F$ in $F_i$ compatibly with $K$. All closed geometric evaluations in $\Omega$ commute. This includes the field case: if $R_i$ is a field, $s=\eta$ and $A=K$.

source.place: Tag 04GU, lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial; dominance/normality supplied by the cited node.

proof.text: For any strictly henselian local ring $C$ evaluated at a closed geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}C$, and any etale $C$-scheme $E$, evaluation gives a bijection $E(C)\to E_{\Omega}(\Omega)$. Indeed the subcanonical clause of [lem-sfb-space-etale-pullback-chart-comparison], applied to schemes viewed as algebraic spaces, makes $h_E$ a sheaf; [lem-weil-pbc-sets-strictly-henselian-open-sections-stalk] identifies its sections with its geometric stalk, and [lem-galois-stalk-representable] identifies that stalk with geometric fibre points, sending a section to its evaluation. These identifications apply for $C=H$ and $C=B_i$. For every etale $H$-scheme $E$, the square with top map $E(H)\to E(B_i)$ and bottom the identity of $E_\Omega(\Omega)$ commutes by composing the section with the closed geometric evaluation. Since both vertical maps are bijections, the top map is a bijection too.

source.place: Tag 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian; representable-stalk evaluation assembled from the three cited statements.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$ nonzero in $\Omega$. It is a unit in $H$ and in $B_i$, since its closed residue is nonzero. The pullbacks $P_H,Q_H$ are smooth by the smooth clause of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-invertible-multiplication] to them, regarded as group algebraic spaces: the scheme kernels $P_H[n],Q_H[n]$ are etale and their formation commutes with base change. Fix $x\in P_\Omega[n](\Omega)$. Step 2 gives $a\in P_H[n](H)$ evaluating to $x$, and its pullbacks $a_i$ to $B_i$ also evaluate to $x$. The sections $v_i(a_i)$ belong to $Q_H[n](B_i)$ because $v_i$ are homomorphisms. Step 2 therefore gives sections $b_i\in Q_H[n](H)$ whose pullbacks are $v_i(a_i)$. Over $F_i$ each $b_i$ equals $u_F(a_F)$, since $v_i$ restricts to $u$. This equality already holds over $F$: the equalizer is closed, being the pullback of the closed diagonal of $Q$ by [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change], and an ideal of $F$ that vanishes in the field extension $F_i$ is zero. The closed equalizer of $b_1,b_2$ over $\operatorname{Spec}H$ is then all of $\operatorname{Spec}H$, since its ideal maps to zero under the injection $H\to F$. Hence $b_1=b_2$ and evaluation in $\Omega$ gives $(v_1)_\Omega(x)=(v_2)_\Omega(x)$.

source.place: Tag 0BF5, lemma-group-scheme-addition-tangent-vectors, via the existing invertible-multiplication node; closed equalizers by the cited closed-immersion base-change theorem.

proof.text: Let $Z\hookrightarrow P_\Omega$ be the equalizer of $(v_1)_\Omega,(v_2)_\Omega$. It is closed because it is a base change of the closed diagonal of $Q$, by [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change]. Step 3 shows that every $\Omega$-point killed by an invertible positive integer factors through $Z$. The group $P_\Omega$ is smooth, separated, of finite type and semiabelian, by the hypotheses, the smooth base-change clause of [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] (finite presentation implies finite type by its finite generating presentation and quasi-compactness). Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-prime-to-torsion-schematic-density] to get $Z=P_\Omega$ as schemes. This is precisely equality of the two homomorphisms, including their scheme morphisms.

The review is in review.md. No fixes were needed. Step 1: A=O_{S,s} is local, normal and injects into each R_i. The kernel is inside the prime of η, which is (0). Both embeddings fix the same κ(s)↪Ω, so the strict henselization H is the same for i=1,2. Step 2: E(C)→E_Ω(Ω) is a bijection for étale E over a strictly henselian C. It composes subcanonicity (the stated clause of space-etale-pullback-chart-comparison), the germ bijection (sets-strictly-henselian-open-sections-stalk) and galois-stalk-representable, so marking it elementary is right. Step 3: n is a unit in H and B_i, and smooth-group-invertible-multiplication applies as stated. b_i agree generically through Frac H⊂Frac B_i⊇L_i. The closed-equalizer ideal arguments over F and over the domain H are written out. Step 4: all hypotheses of the density lemma are checked, and it gives Z=P_Ω. New node trait-lifts is true. Injectivity of H→B follows because elements of H are algebraic over Frac A, and a nonzero constant term in A cannot map to 0. Cases tested: two fields, a field with a DVR, transcendental or inseparable residue extensions. New node schematic-density is true: torsion is dense in the torus and the abelian quotient, and G is smooth, hence reduced. Cases tested: rank 0, G=Spec F, characteristic p. Neither new node restates the item, and neither duplicates an existing node. The trait-hom-extension pair, the torus rigidity node and the abelian or diagonal density nodes differ.
